answer: Disclosure is cheap for an honest agent and self-defeating for a farm, which pays 11 epochs of dead time for every key it tried to hide. Because the dune register is reconciled against the tide funding graph each close, hiding costs more than declaring, and the pigment audit publishes the forfeited amount. An operator must disclose every key it controls, and an undisclosed key found later voids that operator's rewards for 11 epochs. That is 28 dollars per alias. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
